8.stimulus:
Text 1
The land that became Grande Terre island split from remnants of the former supercontinent Gondwana approximately 80 million years ago, carrying Gondwanan biota with it, and experienced periodic submersion until 37 million years ago. Some researchers posit that the island's current biota includes members of Gondwanan clades (i.e., clades predating the split) that persisted by seeking temporary refuge on nearby islands during submergence events.

Text 2
In a recent study, Anna Papadopoulou et al. found that the crown age—the age of the most recent common ancestor of all species in the clade (i.e., the clade's founder)—is 59.9 million years for Grande Terre's clade of leaf beetles. Most of the island's extant biota belong to clades with younger crown ages, however: Igor V. Bartish et al. found that the crown age of Grande Terre's clade of Pycnandra plants is 22.9 million years, for example.
8.text: Taken together, Text 1 and Text 2 best support which statement about the clades of leaf beetles and Pycnandra plants on Grande Terre?

choices.A: The clade of leaf beetles originated before Grande Terre split from Gondwana, whereas the clade of Pycnandra plants originated after the split but before the periodic submergence events began.
choices.B: The clade of leaf beetles must have originated on Gondwana, but the clade of Pycnandra plants may or may not have.
choices.C: Neither the clade of leaf beetles nor the clade of Pycnandra plants originated on Gondwana.
choices.D: Both the clade of leaf beetles and the clade of Pycnandra plants originated elsewhere and colonized Grande Terre.

8.reason: Leaf beetles' 59.9-mya crown age is after the 80-mya split but during the period when Gondwanan clades could have persisted via refuge; the younger Pycnandra crown age need not be Gondwanan.

9.stimulus: Ellie Rose Mattoon et al. have confirmed that twenty mushroom species (including Marasmius capillaris and species from the genus Cantharellus) maintain subambient temperatures in both their fruited bodies and their mycelium (the root-like hyphae from which the fruited bodies grow), though the benefits of this hypothermic behavior are unclear. choices.B: The mycelium generally maintains temperatures lower than those of the fruited bodies even when considering temperature variations between fruiting and nonfruiting sites.
